items.title: Show HN: Plot, a 3D project tracker in your Chrome new tab (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
items.content_text: Hey HN , I made Plot because I kept losing track of my own projects. It's easy nowadays to have 10 vibe-coded projects running simultaneously, but once you have so many projects going on, it's very hard to stay on top of them. You reply to a question Claude asked about Project A, open Project B to debug a little bit, shifting to Project C, build a marketing page, and when you go back to Project A, you've already forget where you left off, what you were going to do next, or why you decided to use that library. I made Plot to help with that. It's a Chrome extension that opens in your new tab, so you can't miss it. Here's what you can do with it: - In the 2D view, you can resize each project's plot. Make the ones you want to focus on bigger, and the others smaller. - In the 3D view, each project is a building. The more tasks you finish and the more decisions and learnings you record, the taller it grows. You can see where you've been putting your effort. - Click into a project to manage its backlog and to-dos, keep a record of what you've shipped, and write down decisions and learnings. Markdown is supported. - In Stats, you can see your recent activity across projects. You can also click a date on the calendar to look back at what you were doing that day. - There's no AI feature in it. Everything is stored locally in your browser. I wanted something lightweight and easy to use that helps me keep track of what I'm building, and looks pretty cool while doing it. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50465656 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

items.title: Show HN: Yogurt - Free, private, open-source alternative to Granola (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
items.content_text: Hey HN, I'm Eric and I want to share an OSS project that I've been building in my free time. Yogurt is a free, MIT licensed desktop app that uses on-device AI models to transcribe, summarize, and chat with your meetings. Here's a quick demo video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BFfbXAwRq98 Similar to Granola, Yogurt runs in the background and does not join your calls. But unlike Granola, Yogurt is open-source, free to use, and private. Your meeting transcripts, call recordings, and summaries never leave your computer. As small OSS models have gotten faster and more powerful, Yogurt seemed like a pretty obvious win for privacy and cost conscious folks. You do not need a frontier model to summarize meeting notes or answer questions about them. And if you want to make your notes available to a frontier model, you can just share it with Anthropic, OpenAI, etc. directly via Yogurt's local MCP server. There's no need to use a paid cloud service as a middleman. I tried some of the most popular OSS note taking tools, and most were missing features like calendar integration, MCP server, etc. or required you to connect or create an account. And more than that, they didn't feel polished enough for it to be something I actually wanted to use daily, and so I built Yogurt to scratch that itch. I spent a lot of time fine-tuning every UI interaction/animation and optimizing the model calls to get the most out of your hardware + make it snappy. To support Windows/Mac/Linux, I decided to go with Electron. I use whisper.cpp for transcription and Apple's on-device SpeechAnalyzer if your system supports it. For call summaries and questions, I use a local open weight LLM that automatically gets downloaded and set up based on what your hardware can handle without your cooling fans firing off like crazy (this part uses llama.cpp). I've spent a lot of time working on details like echo detection/reduction, global/folder/local level search respectively, and auto-end recordings. Hope this is useful for any of you who have held out on using AI note tools for privacy or cost reasons, or for folks using cloud tools who want to switch to something free and open source that still feels great to use. Would love to hear what you think about the onboarding and note taking experience :) Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50454625 Points: 246 # Comments: 95
